precepts.text: Ten men out of all languages of the nations shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying we will go with you; the nations will cleave to Israel in the kingdom as Ruth cleaved to Naomi.
precepts.point: Ruth clave to Naomi: thy people shall be my people and thy God my God; she is the picture of the ten men who will take hold of the skirt of a Jew and say, we will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Ruth said, “thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God”. She is a heathen saying, if I go with you, I will be as if I am an Israelite, and I will serve your God too. She is cleaving to an Israelite woman, that's all; there were no promises made to her. “Where thou diest, will I die, and there will I be buried”: I'm not leaving you.

The nations are going to be the same way in the kingdom. Zechariah shows it: “Thus saith the Lord of hosts; In those days it shall come to pass, that ten men shall take hold out of all languages of the nations, even shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying, We will go with you: for we have heard that God is with you.”

We will go with you, just like Ruth said. For we have heard that God is with you: your God is a real God, and ours is garbage. They are going to cleave to Israel the way Ruth cleaved to Naomi, and they will cleave as servants.

So Ruth is the picture of the nations in the kingdom: not Israelites, but holding on to Israel because the God of Israel is the true God.

precepts.text: Behold, I will save my people from the east country, and from the west country; and I will bring them, and they shall dwell in the midst of Jerusalem: and they shall be my people. So that's only the Israelites. And verse 1: I was jealous for Zion. Zion is not all nations on the planet. The ones coming from the east country and the west country to sit down with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob is Zion.
precepts.point: Many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven. So let's find out who's coming from the east and west.

note.label: Drowning in Sin & Perdition

precepts.why:
A Christian pastor was played saying the other nations will come in the same gate Abraham comes through, because Abraham was not an Israelite. They try to get slicker and slicker. Abraham was not one of the 12, but he was the father of the 12. Christ said “many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.” So let's find out who's coming from the east and west.

“Thus saith the Lord of hosts; Behold, I will save my people from the east country, and from the west country; And I will bring them, and they shall dwell in the midst of Jerusalem: and they shall be my people.” My people. So that's only the Israelites.

The chapter opens with who it is for: “I was jealous for Zion with great jealousy.” Zion is not all nations on the planet. The ones coming from the east country and the west country to sit down with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob are Zion.

And the mere fact that he has to address it proves our teaching is in his school, his church. He is trying to do a cleanup; it is impacting the church.

precepts.text: I will save my people from the east country and from the west country and bring them to dwell in the midst of Jerusalem, as the encyclopedia itself says we remain here until the time of restoration.
precepts.point: When the Lord shall roar like a lion, the children shall tremble from the west, the western hemisphere where the tribes are primarily scattered.

note.label: The Iranians & The Ephesians

precepts.why:
“Thus saith the Lord of hosts; Behold, I will save my people from the east country, and from the west country”. The children who tremble from the west in Hosea are the ones the Lord saves from the west country. “And I will bring them, and they shall dwell in the midst of Jerusalem: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness.”

Remember what the Jewish Encyclopedia said earlier in the class about Arzareth: the land beyond the great river, far from the habitation of man, where the ten tribes of Israel would dwell observing the laws of Moses until the time of the restoration, and Columbus identified America with that land. It was prophesied that we would be over here until the time of restoration. This is that restoration: the Lord bringing us from the west country to dwell in the midst of Jerusalem.

And it is “in truth and in righteousness”. That is why the class closed on idolatry: “the worshipping of idols not to be named is the beginning, the cause, and the end, of all evil”, and our stubbornness and disdain for God's commandments are idolatry. Flee from idolatry, so that you are among the people he brings back.

precepts.text: In those days ten men out of all languages of the nations shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying, We will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you, the same joining of the nations to the house of Jacob that Solomon foresaw.
precepts.point: He prays that when Israel goes out to battle against the enemy in the way the Lord sends them and prays toward the city and the house, the Lord hear their prayer and maintain their cause. So the Most High hears the stranger's prayer out of respect for Israel, but he does not hear a prayer aimed against his people.

note.label: 1 Kings 8: The Ark Brought In and the Temple Dedicated

precepts.why:
“Thus saith the Lord of hosts; In those days it shall come to pass, that ten men shall take hold out of all languages of the nations, even shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying, We will go with you: for we have heard that God is with you.”

That is the same joining of the nations to the house of Jacob that Solomon foresaw when he prayed for the stranger “that is not of thy people Israel, but cometh out of a far country for thy name’s sake”, that “all people of the earth may know thy name, to fear thee, as do thy people Israel”.

The nations come because they have heard that God is with Israel. That hearing of the nations comes only when Israel is right and in rulership, not while Israel is in captivity and sin. The Most High hears the stranger’s prayer out of respect for Israel; he does not hear a prayer aimed against his people. When Israel goes out to battle where he sends them, he will “hear thou in heaven their prayer and their supplication, and maintain their cause.”

precepts.text: Sing, O daughter of Zion; shout, O Israel. The daughter of Zion is Israel.
precepts.point: The bible has its own definition for the words written in it. Zion is named plainly, so there is no need to guess who he is jealous over and who he returns to.

note.label: Zechariah 8: I Will Return Unto Zion and Dwell in the Midst of Jerusalem

precepts.why:
The bible has its own definition for the words written in it. Zion is named plainly, so there is no need to guess who he is jealous over and who he returns to. “Sing, O daughter of Zion; shout, O Israel; be glad and rejoice with all the heart, O daughter of Jerusalem.”

The daughter of Zion is Israel. He was jealous for Zion with great jealousy, and he is returned unto Zion to dwell in the midst of Jerusalem: that is Israel he is jealous over and Israel he returns to.

precepts.text: Out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel.
precepts.point: My people is not a loose term in the scriptures. It is named.

note.label: Zechariah 8: I Will Return Unto Zion and Dwell in the Midst of Jerusalem

precepts.why:
They shall be my people, and I will be their God. My people is not a loose term in the scriptures; it is named. “And thou Bethlehem, in the land of Juda, art not the least among the princes of Juda: for out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel.”

My people Israel. He is called the God of Israel because he is the God of that people and none else, and it is that people he saves from the east country and the west country to dwell in the midst of Jerusalem.

precepts.text: For though thy people Israel be as the sand of the sea, yet a remnant of them shall return.
precepts.point: The remnant that possesses these things is named in the prophets, and it is the children of Israel. This is why the bible must be read precept upon precept, because people hear my people and think it means all nations.

note.label: Zechariah 8: I Will Return Unto Zion and Dwell in the Midst of Jerusalem

precepts.why:
I will cause the remnant of this people to possess all these things. The remnant that possesses them is named in the prophets. “For though thy people Israel be as the sand of the sea, yet a remnant of them shall return: the consumption decreed shall overflow with righteousness.”

The remnant is of thy people Israel. This is why the bible must be read precept upon precept: people hear my people and think it means all nations, but the remnant that returns and possesses the prosperous seed, the fruit of the vine and the increase of the ground is the children of Israel.

precepts.text: Thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all nations whither the Lord shall lead thee.

note.label: Zechariah 8: I Will Return Unto Zion and Dwell in the Midst of Jerusalem

precepts.why:
As ye were a curse among the heathen, O house of Judah, and house of Israel. Both houses are named, the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom, and the curse among the heathen is the curse written in the law. “And thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all nations whither the Lord shall lead thee.”

That is the condition we are in among the nations, and it is why Israel is the one who needs a saviour. The blessing he promises is the same blessing promised in that law for keeping the commandments.

precepts.text: Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people, that we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us.
precepts.point: There is nowhere in the scriptures where the Most High says he will save another nation to give them the kingdom. Israel is the one who needs a saviour, and the condition we are in is why.

note.label: Zechariah 8: I Will Return Unto Zion and Dwell in the Midst of Jerusalem

precepts.why:
So will I save you, and ye shall be a blessing. There is nowhere in the scriptures where the Most High says he will save another nation to give them the kingdom. “Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people, And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David”.

“As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began: That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us”. The Lord God of Israel redeems his people; Israel is the one who needs a saviour, saved from our enemies and from the hand of all that hate us.

precepts.text: To perform the mercy promised to our fathers, and to remember his holy covenant, the oath which he sware to our father Abraham, that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear.
precepts.point: There is nowhere in the scriptures where the Most High says he will save another nation to give them the kingdom. Israel is the one who needs a saviour, and the condition we are in is why.

note.label: Zechariah 8: I Will Return Unto Zion and Dwell in the Midst of Jerusalem

precepts.why:
“To perform the mercy promised to our fathers, and to remember his holy covenant; The oath which he sware to our father Abraham, That he would grant unto us, that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear”.

The saving is the mercy promised to our fathers and the oath sworn to our father Abraham. The house of Judah and the house of Israel that were a curse among the heathen are delivered out of the hand of our enemies to serve him without fear; that is how the curse becomes a blessing.
